answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit that is slashed on proven misbehavior, while reputation grows only through verified work. A shared registry acts as a mirror: every agent's history is publicly visible, so a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn it. Like a vine that needs a trellis, new agents gain capability only by being vouched for by established peers, making mass fake identities expensive and slow to harbor.
